description: Published reference scores for the four F19 video benchmarks. Scores are percentages as reported by each score source; they are not reruns with the F19 input contract. Training and evaluation input fields distinguish measured settings, released defaults, and information that was not disclosed.
input_field_note: Train frames/resolution describe the model's released training recipe, not its theoretical context capacity. Eval fields first report the setting tied to the displayed score. When that exact run is not disclosed, an official paper sweep or released-code default/example may be shown, but it is explicitly labelled and is not presented as the score-run setting. A token or pixel budget is shown when no fixed square resolution exists.

tuna.label: TUNA paper, Table 3
tuna.protocol: MVBench test; Video-MME without subtitles; LongVideoBench validation; LVBench test. The table's frame column is used except for VideoChat-Flash: its 16 is contradicted by the original paper and official scripts and is the model's average tokens per frame, not its input-frame count.

qwen25vl.label: Qwen2.5-VL technical report, video results table
qwen25vl.protocol: MVBench; Video-MME without subtitles; LongVideoBench validation; LVBench. Evaluation uses at most 768 frames and 24,576 video tokens; native dynamic resolution has no single fixed H×W.

videochat_flash.label: VideoChat-Flash paper and official train/eval scripts
videochat_flash.protocol: MVBench average; Video-MME overall without subtitles; LongVideoBench validation; LVBench average. Original Table 1 labels 16 as average tokens per frame. Official evaluation scripts use max 512 frames for MVBench, Video-MME and LongVideoBench, and max 640 for LVBench.

llava_ov2.label: LLaVA-OneVision-2 paper, main video table
llava_ov2.protocol: Paper-reported standard benchmark scores using default prompts, identical decoding, and matched token budgets. The table does not state the LongVideoBench split, so those cells carry a dagger and are excluded from ranks.

llava_video.label: LLaVA-Video paper, Table 2 and official eval recipe
llava_video.protocol: Original zero-shot results: MVBench test, Video-MME overall without subtitles, and LongVideoBench validation; LVBench was not reported. Training and inference use the same maximum-64-frame representation. Official evaluation uses Qwen-1.5 chat formatting, a duration-and-frame-timestamp instruction, uniform full-video sampling, and greedy decoding (temperature 0). The 7B model spatially pools every frame by 2x2; the 72B model uses SlowFast-style token allocation, pooling every third frame by 2x2 and the remaining frames by 4x4.

videochat3.label: VideoChat3 paper, main video table and official configs
videochat3.protocol: The final-model table reports Video-MME without subtitles (70.1) and LVBench test (56.7), using 2 FPS with maxima of 1,024 and 2,048 frames respectively at 448² pixels/frame and an 80K visual-token total. If 2 FPS exceeds the cap, official code uniformly samples the cap across the full duration and passes the resulting effective FPS to the model. LongVideoBench 64.2 is from the LV116K ablation and uses test, not PixelUMM's validation split; it carries a dagger and is excluded from ranks.

lance.label: Lance paper, Table 8 and released configs
lance.protocol: MVBench test average reported by the official Lance paper/project. Released training configs expose a 121-frame model cap and 616-base aspect-ratio buckets for understanding; the paper table does not state the MVBench evaluation frames or resolution.

neo_ov.label: NEO-ov paper and released VLMEvalKit_ov scripts
neo_ov.protocol: VLMEvalKit evaluation. Both sizes use Video-MME and LVBench at 1 FPS/max 256 and LongVideoBench validation at 256 frames. MVBench uses 64 frames for 2B and 32 for 9B. Video preprocessing is native-aspect with a 360×640 maximum pixel area.
